sents.t: After my decision, Lily started acting strangely.
She canceled our movie night twice.
When I came into the café, she quickly closed her laptop.
“She must be planning something,” Carlos said.
“Or she might be upset with me,” I worried.
“She can’t be upset,” Ana said.
“She smiled all night at my party.”
On Thursday, I saw her coming out of a bank downtown with a man in a suit.
She looked excited.
“He must work at the bank,” I thought.
“But why does she need a bank?”
On Saturday, Priya called me.
“Can you come to the old flower shop on Oak Street at ten? Don’t tell Lily I called.”
When I arrived, the door was open.
Inside, Lily was standing in the middle of the room with paint on her hands and a huge smile.
“Surprise!” she said.
“I’ve been working on this for months. I got a small business loan. This is going to be my bakery!”
Suddenly, everything made sense: the laptop, the bank, the paint.
“I wanted to wait until you decided about Chicago,” she said.
“Now we both get to stay.”
I hugged her, paint and all.
I was so proud.

o: She was opening her own bakery.
She had a new job at a bank.
Sam understood the reasons for her behavior.
